title: Cleveland Guardians Face Player Injuries Amid Playoff Push
text:
Trending Story
Updated 04:39 AM UTC, Thu September 25, 2025
Cleveland Guardians Face Player Injuries Amid Playoff Push
CLEVELAND, Ohio — Ballplayers have to be nimble because they can be in one place today and another tomorrow. The Guardians, on the verge of the postseason, have lost two players from their 26-man roster to season-ending injuries in the last four days. Outfielder Nolan Jones was lost to a strained right oblique muscle during Saturday’s day-night doubleheader against the Twins and DH David Fry was hit in the face on Tuesday night in the sixth inning against the Tigers.
Jakob Junis
"Off the field, he’s our team leader. He’s the face of the clubhouse. He’s kind of what makes this engine go. We all kind of rally around him and the morale he brings every day. It’s a winning baseball attitude."
Daniel Schneeman
"The way he leads this clubhouse is a huge part of our success. The way he leads our meetings. He gives great advice to the young guys, the old guys."
Stephen Vogt
"He’s always talking to the dugout. He’s talking with the starters who aren’t pitching. He’s talking with the other hitters. He’s actively engaged in chatter and keeping our guys focused. He’s a great leader, great teammate. He pushes everyone around him to get better."
